scan_metadata.paper_name: Full-Order Sampling-Based MPC for Torque-Level Locomotion Control via Diffusion-Style Annealing (DIAL-MPC)
scan_metadata.explanation: No user filter; whole repository considered (129 tracked files: 25 Python files, 10 example YAML files, README, setup.py, one CI workflow, MuJoCo model assets). There are no notebooks, no tests (the pytest step in .github/workflows/python-package.yml:38-40 is commented out), no docs directory and no stored reference outputs. The user interface is six console scripts (setup.py:23-32). One of them, `dial-mpc`, is a bounded headless file-producing operation and yields two proposed tools; the seven packaged synchronous examples are merged into one rollout tool, with four assigned for execution and three kept as optional supporting examples. Asynchronous simulation, real-robot deployment and the two helper entry points are deferred or omitted with concrete blockers. Selection does not establish that execution passes on the 8 GB GPU / 7.5 GB RAM machine; the environment result decides feasibility and problem size.
scan_metadata.paths_note: `path` is relative to the repository checkout repo/dial-mpc; `project_path` is relative to the project root. sha256 values were computed from the checkout at scan time with sha256sum.

tool_review.task: Simulate a robot under closed-loop DIAL-MPC control for n_steps control steps and obtain the executed state/control trajectory, the planner's predicted link trajectories and an interactive HTML visualization.

implementation.equivalence: `--example NAME` only resolves NAME + '.yaml' inside the package and loads it with yaml.safe_load; `--config FILE` loads FILE the same way (dial_core.py:206-209). Everything after that is shared.

source_lines.environment_creation: dial_core.py:220-227; registries dial_mpc/envs/__init__.py:14-22 and unitree_go2_env.py:806-808, unitree_h1_env.py:904-906, manipulation.py:117
source_lines.outputs: dial_core.py:270-271 (stdout mean reward), 277-281 (output dir and timestamp), 293-302 (HTML), 305-323 (states and predictions arrays)

inputs.selection: Exactly one of `example` (packaged name) or `config_path` (user YAML). Resolve user paths to absolute before changing the subprocess working directory.

typed_overrides_recommended.name: seed
typed_overrides_recommended.note: Seeds the JAX PRNG for reset and sampling. Run-to-run repeatability on the GPU must be measured by the executor before any promise is made.

typed_overrides_recommended.name: n_steps
typed_overrides_recommended.note: Number of control steps; each is 0.02 s in all packaged examples (dt).

typed_overrides_recommended.name: Nsample
typed_overrides_recommended.note: Parallel sampled rollouts per diffusion iteration; main memory lever.

typed_overrides_recommended.name: Hnode
typed_overrides_recommended.note: Number of spline control nodes minus one.

typed_overrides_recommended.name: Ndiffuse
typed_overrides_recommended.note: Annealing iterations per control step after the first.

typed_overrides_recommended.name: Ndiffuse_init
typed_overrides_recommended.note: Annealing iterations at the first step.

typed_overrides_recommended.name: default_vx / default_vy / default_vyaw
typed_overrides_recommended.upstream: UnitreeGo2EnvConfig unitree_go2_env.py:29-31; UnitreeH1WalkEnvConfig unitree_h1_env.py:73-75; UnitreeH1LocoEnvConfig unitree_h1_env.py:602-604
typed_overrides_recommended.note: Commanded base velocity. Effective only in env unitree_go2_walk, unitree_h1_walk, unitree_h1_push_crate, unitree_h1_loco (used at unitree_go2_env.py:142-146 and the matching H1 code).

typed_overrides_recommended.name: ramp_up_time
typed_overrides_recommended.note: Seconds over which the velocity command ramps from zero.

typed_overrides_recommended.name: gait
typed_overrides_recommended.note: Go2: stand, walk, trot, canter, gallop. H1: stand, slow_walk, walk, jog. An unknown name fails upstream with KeyError when the step function is traced.

typed_overrides_recommended.name: jump_dt
typed_overrides_recommended.note: Seconds per jump stage; env unitree_go2_seq_jump only.

typed_overrides_recommended.name: pose_target_sequence
typed_overrides_recommended.note: Base position target per stage; env unitree_go2_seq_jump only.

typed_overrides_recommended.name: yaw_target_sequence
typed_overrides_recommended.note: Yaw target per stage, same length as pose_target_sequence (assert at unitree_go2_env.py:567).

inputs.config_file_only: leg_control, kp, kd, action_scale, dt, timestep, backend, debug, task_name, randomize_tasks, contact_targets, contact_target_radius: defined by the dataclasses but tied to the model files (the Go2/H1 scenes use torque actuators; Allegro implements only position control, manipulation.py:68-71) or unused by the packaged examples. They stay reachable through `config_path`; no typed parameter proposed.
inputs.not_exposed: update_method (only `mppi` exists, dial_core.py:57-59); env_name as an override (it decides which other keys are valid; change it through `config_path`); output_dir (set by the wrapper to a fresh per-call directory, since file names depend only on a one-second timestamp, dial_core.py:281).
inputs.source_backed_contract_check: Because load_dataclass_from_dict silently drops keys that the target dataclass does not define (io_utils.py:16), an override for a field that the selected env's config class does not have would be ignored without error. The wrapper should reject such an override, using the field lists of the dataclasses cited above, rather than return a result that looks as if the parameter had been applied.
inputs.custom_environment: `--custom-env MODULE` (dial_core.py:188-193, 202-204) imports MODULE from the working directory. See the separate candidate below; not part of the default parameter set.

files: <output_dir>/<ts>_states.npy : shape (n_steps, 1 + nq + nv + nu), row = [step index, qpos, qvel, ctrl] (dial_core.py:305-322)

<output_dir>/<ts>_predictions.npy : shape (n_steps, Hsample+1, n_links, 3), reward-weighted mean of predicted link positions from the last annealing iteration of each step (dial_core.py:124, 135, 319-323)
native_outputs.stdout: `mean reward = <value in %.2e>` (dial_core.py:270-271); progress bars go to stderr (tqdm).
native_outputs.write_timing: All files are written only after the whole rollout has finished; an interrupted run leaves nothing.

tool_review.process_handling: The command never exits by itself because of `app.run(port=5000)` (dial_core.py:329). Proposed handling without touching upstream code: set FLASK_RUN_FROM_CLI=true in the child environment, which makes Flask.run return immediately (flask/app.py:611 in the project environment, flask 3.1.1 at scan time), so the process ends with status 0 and port 5000 is never opened. Fallback: poll for `*_predictions.npy`, then SIGINT (werkzeug/serving.py:817-823 swallows KeyboardInterrupt). If port 5000 is busy the unmodified command exits non-zero after the artifacts are already written. Whichever mechanism is used must be the one the executor actually observed.

verification_source.basis: Direct standalone execution of the documented commands (execution assignments in reports/tutorial-scanner-include-in-tools.json). The repository ships no expected outputs, so the reference is the executor's retained run on the same config and seed.
verification_source.compared: Exit status; one file of each kind; dtypes and shapes; step-index column; finiteness; mean reward from stdout; maximum absolute difference of both arrays between wrapper call and standalone command at the same seed, with a tolerance taken from the executor's same-seed replay.
verification_source.changed_input_checks: n_steps changes the row count exactly; a different seed changes the arrays; default_vx changes the reached base displacement in the commanded direction (property of the velocity-tracking reward, unitree_go2_env.py:214), each confirmed by an independent direct `dial-mpc --config` run.
verification_source.failure_checks: `--example` with an unknown name fails at dial_core.py:207 before any compilation; neither/both of example and config_path; a gait name not in the env's table; a typed override not defined for the env; timeout.

tool_review.feasibility_notes: Memory grows with (Nsample+1) x (Hsample+1) simulator states per annealing iteration (dial_core.py:114-120); all examples use Nsample 2048. Whether these fit an 8 GB GPU and 7.5 GB RAM is for the environment manager and executors to establish; any reduction must go through the config fields above and be recorded.

notes_for_environment_and_executors: Install mode: setup.py:7 uses find_packages(include=["dial_mpc"]), which matches only the top-level package, and package_data is keyed by "dial-mpc" (setup.py:22). A non-editable install would therefore miss the subpackages, models and example YAML files; the README's editable install from the checkout (README.md:57) is the layout to keep and to document for delivery.
flask is imported at dial_core.py:290, after the rollout and before any file is written, but is not listed in setup.py; it arrives through brax. Without it a run would lose all results.
dial_mpc/utils and dial_mpc/models/* have no __init__.py; get_model_path relies on importlib.resources with namespace packages (io_utils.py:5-7).
dial_core.py:31-33 appends `--xla_gpu_triton_gemm_any=True` to XLA_FLAGS on import; whether the installed jaxlib accepts that flag is something the first real run shows.

Dependencies are unpinned upstream; at scan time the project environment contained brax 0.12.3, jax/jaxlib 0.6.1, mujoco and mujoco_mjx 3.3.2, numpy 1.26.4, flask 3.1.1, werkzeug 3.1.3 (directory listing only, nothing executed by the scanner).
MBDPI fixes its control period to 0.02 s (dial_core.py:74) regardless of the config `dt`; all packaged examples use dt 0.02.
The scanner executed no repository command; every statement above comes from reading the cited lines.

Should the three unassigned synchronous examples (h1_loco, h1_push_crate, go2_crate_climb) get executors, or be documented as accepted but not executed here?
Should --custom-env be exposed on the strength of a re-registration check only, or stay deferred?
Is dial_mpc_list_examples wanted as a separate tool, or should its names be folded into the rollout tool's parameter documentation?
